brief: Berit's open box in the tent: thin brown book, small tin pot with bent handle, shapeless green hat, dented bucket; a mitted hand reaches for the bucket.
A spade has just uncovered a ring of old fitted stones: the dry old well, one notch worn smooth at child height; an empty crate beside it.
A real thumb-sized hammer, worn shiny, lies in the corner of the new barn where the last bundle must go; tiny footprints in the sawdust.
The finished pine barn at dusk with a lantern hung on a post outside, well away from the barn door.
The farm's own windmill with four new sails groans and begins to turn in a strong wind.
A small paper slip with wavy lines and one tiny wavy line in the corner, held in mitts beside a scorched half-burnt page; a lit lantern on the gatepost behind.
The village waits wet in a squall on the Landing Steps for the family's barge; an old woman with a stick looks out.
At the Fair tent, long-legged children run past towards the pony while Granny Maud presses a steaming bowl into a man's hands.
The plain grey Fair cloth with tiny moons along its edge, the empty stool at its head; Elder Agnes guards it.
A big chalk board covered with seven years of thin chalk moons stands on the Pie Table; the baker holds a wet cloth and nobody moves.
Fair evening: a lantern rolls away by the straw bales, the bunny's ears thump under the table, the alpaca hums, a mitted hand reaches for the lantern.
End of the Fair: Captain Mei stands on the end of the table calling the roll and the whole village shouts back.
A goat with no collar goes for the weed pile; Granny Maud stops short, staring at the green hat on the fence post.
Rue the market seller at her cart on the dry road, flour sack on the tailboard, a bag of coins in her hand, a sly smile.
Dusk: a bucket of water on top of the burnt gatepost beside a row of small grey stones; an old woman and a goat walk away.
Twin children, boy and girl with the same freckles, dare each other to touch the burnt gatepost; hungry and very brave.
Tom the shepherd boy shivers at the stick fence with nine sheep around his legs; a mitted hand passes a glowing log over the fence with tongs.
Longnight: the village lights are out except the Hall; Lark sits on the farm fence with a lantern and a bowl, seen from behind.
A loaf with a thin chalk moon on its crust; Greenstem looks at it sadly with a bunch of sage.
Greenstem, eyes shut, holds half a fresh loaf in both hands and breathes the steam in.
A shaggy grey goat with one bent horn and no collar chews the list (wavy lines only) while Lark holds up a finger.
Thorne, the Lord's round brown gardener, comes up the road with a bundle of apple twigs tied with blank paper tags, glancing back.
Pieter the night watchman sits on the fence in daylight, lantern still lit, holding out a small tin flask.
At the forest edge, thyme bundles on a crate; Lark bows politely to a huge oak with a hollow and one tiny bell.
First-person: mitted hands hold a scrap of sack with a burnt wheel mark and a folded note in round quick scribble, beside a loaf.

brief: Landing Day: Mei waves a thick folded letter high from the barge deck.
An empty clean pickle jar on a table with a pressed leaf, a brass button and a small folded paper in a round hand (wavy lines).
A folded letter on the kitchen table beside a honey jar, a sprig of thyme and a pot; a barge far off through the window.
The new barn's bare frame against an evening sky, like the ribs of something asleep.
A cobbled road of round stones in the rain, water running into the ditch; Hazelwood far off; a cart parked.
First-person: mitted hands hold up a lopsided steaming flatbread, a bit burnt at one edge, beside the stone quern.
Snow: the one green patch with prints three times round it, stopping at the forest edge.
Inside the greenhouse: warm green air, the first red tomato, the farmer's green hat hung beside it.
The first water seeps into the new pond: dark patch, shine, a sky with clouds lying on the ground.
Forest edge by day: white stones half sunk in moss, an old oak with faded ribbons, a mitted hand resting on one stone.
A small stream carries white paper-petalled flowers round a bend into the forest.
White paper-petalled flowers tied with thread on the still-room doorstep; Wren turns them over, puzzled.
